Class IuEntityDao<K,I,E>

java.lang.Object
edu.iu.dao.IuEntityDao<K,I,E>
Type Parameters:
K - key type
I - contract interface type
E - entity type
public abstract class IuEntityDao<K,I,E> extends Object
Abstract base class for a DAO resource with load, search, save, and delete operations.

Operations are suitable for a keyed collection: load(Object) reads one row, search(Map, Search) lists a range, save(Object, Object) writes one row whole, merge(Object, K, I) applies a partial input to one row, and delete(Object) removes one. A subclass names the key type K, the contract interface I its callers read and write, and the entity type E that stores it.

Entity decorators

The entity opts in to the behavior it needs by implementing decorator interfaces; an entity that doesn't implement one is left untouched by the corresponding operation. SaveableEntity takes a full input in save, MergeableEntity takes a partial input in merge, and SequencedEntity takes the position of a child row saved or merged as part of a child collection.

Hooks

Related rows are handled by overriding afterLoad(E), afterSave(I, E), afterMerge(I, E), beforeDelete(E) and afterDelete(E); beforeInput(I, E) and afterInput(I, E) surround the application of input to an entity, and afterInput(I, E) is where a subclass prepares an entity to be written, i.e., stamps audit columns. The four input-related hooks receive the input given to the save or merge, which is null when the caller passed none, so a parent DAO can read its child collection from it.

Writes

A save applies its input onto the row already stored under that key when there is one, so columns the input does not carry -- when the row was created, which parent it belongs to -- survive an update. A merge applies only the values a partial input carries.

Parent and child rows

A child DAO maintains the rows that belong to a parent entity from within the parent DAO's afterSave(I, E) or afterMerge(I, E) hook, by passing the input's child collection to save(Iterable) or merge(Iterable). The child DAO finds the parent through parent() and the parent's input through the input argument of its afterSave(I, E) or afterMerge(I, E) hook, and opts in by overriding search(Search) to select the parent's stored children. Because a parent-driven search decides which stored rows are deleted, the default implementation returns no rows, and a child collection is then saved or merged without removing anything. delete() removes all of the parent's children, by default those search() returns. Every verb is strict about the parent: unless the entity implements ChildEntity, or the DAO overrides tryBinding(Object, E) (or bind(Object, E)) to accept it, an operation on a DAO while a parent is active throws IllegalArgumentException. A new row is bound to the parent when created, before input is applied, and a stored row is bound again on load, save, merge and delete, so a stored child of a different parent is rejected. withParent(Object, Runnable) and the overloads that take a parent object inject one without a hook.

An entity class should override hashCode, equals and toString over its primary key values, as the rejection message identifies the child by its toString.

Listing

Search reads every matching row, orders them by order(), and populates related rows for the requested range only. Range and order operations are suitable only for tables backed by a caching DAO with fewer than 10k rows.

Access from sibling DAOs

The key methods are protected, so a DAO in another package than this class may not call them on a sibling DAO. A family of DAOs that do so, such as a parent generating keys for a child's rows, redeclares them in a common base class in its own package.

    • parent

      protected Object parent()
      Gets the parent entity last noted by a load, save, merge, or delete operation on the current thread.

      The value is set to the entity being operated on while the afterLoad(E), afterSave(I, E), afterMerge(I, E), beforeDelete(E), and afterDelete(E) hooks run, and restored when the hook returns. The value is shared by all DAOs on the thread, so a child DAO invoked from one of those hooks sees the parent DAO's entity, and MAY cast it to the parent entity type.

      Returns:
      parent entity; null when no such hook is running

    • tryBinding

      protected boolean tryBinding(Object parent, E child)
      Tries binding a child entity to a given parent.

      Used by search(IuEntityDao.Search) to filter results by parent(), and by the default bind(Object, E) to reject an entity that does not implement ChildEntity. Delegates to ChildEntity.tryBinding(Object) when child implements ChildEntity; else returns true only when parent is null. A DAO whose entity does not implement ChildEntity may override only this method to accept a parent; bind(Object, E) need not be overridden.

      Implementations MAY initialize a child entity binding, and SHOULD be non-destructive and fail fast.

      Parameters:
      parent - parent to validate against
      child - child entity
      Returns:
      true if the child is, or has just been, bound to the parent; false if it cannot be bound to the parent

    • bind

      protected void bind(Object parent, E child)
      Binds child to a given parent.

      Invoked with parent() by newEntity(K) for a new row, and by load(Object, K) (and so merge(Object, K, I)), save(Object, K, I) and delete(Object, K) for a stored row, before any hook runs. Delegates to ChildEntity.bind(Object) when child implements ChildEntity; else throws IllegalArgumentException unless tryBinding(Object, E) accepts the parent. Strict by default: a DAO supports a parent by one of

      1. an entity that implements ChildEntity,
      2. overriding tryBinding(Object, E) to accept the parent, or
      3. overriding this method, which may also record the parent on the child.

      Otherwise a save or merge from a parent DAO's afterSave(I, E) or afterMerge(I, E) fails with IllegalArgumentException.

      The message of the exception includes the parent and the child's Object.toString(). As a best practice, an entity class should override hashCode, equals and toString over its primary key values, so the message identifies the row.

      Parameters:
      parent - parent to bind to; null when no parent is active
      child - child entity
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the child cannot be bound to the parent

    • afterSave

      protected void afterSave(I input, E entity)
      Performs secondary writes after the row itself is saved.

      This event is invoked by save(Object, K, I) after IuDao.saveBean(Object) completes successfully. Only this method or afterMerge(I, E) will be invoked, not both.

      Related values are read from the input rather than from the entity: an entity only takes its own columns from the input, so a child collection the input carries is not on the entity.

      entity - entity as saved

    • search

      protected List<E> search(IuEntityDao.Search<E> search)
      Eagerly searches for entities by criteria defined by parent reference.

      MAY be invoked from within a parent DAO's afterLoad(E), afterSave(I, E), afterMerge(I, E), or afterDelete(E) method to look up child rows.

      Subclasses opt in to parent-driven search by overriding this method; by default no rows are returned. Because the result decides which stored child rows are deleted by save(Iterable), an override must select only rows that belong to parent().

      Parameters:
      search - parent, filter and range, as captured from parent() by IuEntityDao.Search.child() and its sibling factories
      Returns:
      results, in order(); by default, empty

    • save

      public K save(K key, I input) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException
      Saves an entity.

      This method differs from merge(Object, K, I) in two ways. Null values in the input clear the existing value, where merge preserves it. And when no entity is stored under the key, a new entity is created, where merge requires an existing row.

      For an existing row, afterLoad(E) is invoked after the entity bean is read and before beforeInput(I, E), with parent() set to the entity; a new entity is not loaded, so neither hook is invoked. The input is then applied by SaveableEntity.save(I), when the entity implements it, and the sequence number is injected, when the entity implements SequencedEntity and the save is part of a child collection. A null input is allowed, and is passed to the hooks as given.

      An existing row is bound to parent() by bind(Object, E) before any hook runs. A new row is created by newEntity(K), which binds the active parent before the input is applied. A child that cannot be bound is an IllegalArgumentException, never an EntityNotFoundException, and nothing is written. The sequence number is injected after the input is applied and before afterInput(I, E).

      Parameters:
      key - key to save the input as; may be null if the key is provided by passing input to key(Object)
      input - input properties
      Returns:
      key under which the input was saved; the key as given, else the key carried by the input, else a generated key
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the entity is not a valid child of the active parent, or both key and the key carried by input are non-null and not equal
      UnsupportedOperationException - if neither key nor input provides a key, and key generation is not supported

    • save

      public void save(Iterable<? extends I> children)
      Saves all child rows.

      Intended to be invoked from the parent DAO's afterSave(I, E) or afterMerge(I, E) hook. The keys of the rows search() returns, if any, are bound to a set and removed as child rows are saved. Any keys left over (not saved as a child row) are then deleted. With the default search(Search), nothing is deleted.

      When the entity type implements SequencedEntity, the position of each child in the collection, starting at 0, is injected before the child is saved.

      Parameters:
      children - child collection; null to leave stored child rows unchanged

    • merge

      public K merge(Object parent, K key, I input) throws EntityNotFoundException, IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException
      Merges a partial input onto a stored entity.

      This method differs from save in two ways. Null values in the input preserve the existing value, where save clears it. And merge requires an existing row, loaded through load(Object) so that afterLoad(E) is invoked, which facilitates appending or modifying specific related values.

      The input is applied by MergeableEntity.merge(I), when the entity implements it, and the sequence number is injected, when the entity implements SequencedEntity and the merge is part of a child collection. A null input is allowed, and is passed to the hooks as given.

      Parameters:
      parent - parent object
      key - of the row to merge with; may be null if the key is provided by passing input to key(Object)
      input - partial input, naming the key of a stored entity
      Returns:
      key of the row the input was merged with
      Throws:
      EntityNotFoundException - if no entity is stored under the key
      IllegalArgumentException - if the entity is not a valid child of the active parent, or both key and the key carried by input are non-null and not equal
      NullPointerException - if neither key nor input provides a key

    • merge

      public K merge(K key, I input) throws EntityNotFoundException, IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException
      Merges a partial input onto a stored entity: the alternative to save for PATCH.

      This method differs from save in two ways. Null values in the input preserve the existing value, where save clears it. And merge requires an existing row, loaded through load(Object) so that afterLoad(E) is invoked, which facilitates appending or modifying specific related values.

      The input is applied by MergeableEntity.merge(I), when the entity implements it, and the sequence number is injected, when the entity implements SequencedEntity and the merge is part of a child collection. A null input is allowed, and is passed to the hooks as given.

      The entity is bound to parent() by bind(Object, E) as it is loaded, before any hook runs; a child that cannot be bound is an IllegalArgumentException, never an EntityNotFoundException. The sequence number is injected after the input is applied and before afterInput(I, E), as in save.

      Parameters:
      key - of the row to merge with; may be null if the key is provided by passing input to key(Object)
      input - partial input, naming the key of a stored entity
      Returns:
      key of the row the input was merged with
      Throws:
      EntityNotFoundException - if no entity is stored under the key
      IllegalArgumentException - if the entity is not a valid child of the active parent, or both key and the key carried by input are non-null and not equal
      NullPointerException - if neither key nor input provides a key

      public K merge(I input)

    • merge

      public void merge(Object parent, Iterable<? extends I> children)
      Merges all child rows.

      The collection is validated before anything is written. Stored child rows are visited in the order search() returns them; those the collection names are merged, and new children are then saved in the order given. When the entity type implements SequencedEntity, every stored row is given its position in that order, including rows the collection does not name (those are merged with no input), and each new child takes the next position after the stored rows. Rows that need no change are expected to be skipped by IuDao.saveBean(Object), though their hooks still run.

      Parameters:
      parent - parent object
      children - child collection; null to leave stored child rows unchanged
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if two children carry the same key, or a child carries a key that is not among the stored child rows

      public void merge(Iterable<? extends I> children)
      Merges all child rows.

      Intended to be invoked from the parent DAO's afterMerge(I, E) hook. Children that carry a key are merged onto the stored child row with that key, as found by search(); children that carry no key are saved as new rows. Stored child rows not named in the collection keep their values.

      The collection is validated before anything is written.       public void delete(Object parent, K key)
      Deletes an entity, if one exists under the key.

      Invokes beforeDelete(E), deletes the row, then invokes afterDelete(E), without invoking afterLoad(E). Does nothing when no entity is stored under the key.

      Parameters:
      parent - parent object
      key - key
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the entity is not a valid child of the active parent, as determined by bind(Object, E)
